title: Early HATS-70 fits do not separate a triangular dip from four harmonics in two later TESS sectors
abstract: We test the known 0.814-day signal near HATS-70. We fit three early TESS sectors and predict two later sectors. We use the published residual data and the previously selected period band. A triangular dip reduces later weighted squared error by 45.2 relative to a constant. A four-harmonic fit reduces it by 51.6. The triangle advantage over four harmonics is -6.4; a daily-block bootstrap gives a 95 percent range from -34.9 to 22.3. Separate sector exclusions favor the triangle, so the shape ranking depends on the data split. The test supports a repeat signal in these processed data but does not separate an eclipse from coherent smooth variation. It does not confirm a planet, identify the source star, or exclude an instrumental cause. We supply new code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and repeat instructions. The source cadence data stay outside this package.

display.caption: Early fits predict the last two sectors. A triangle and a four-harmonic model give similar prediction scores. Separate sector exclusions favor the triangle. All tests use the same prior residual product.

citations.reason: Source of the HATS-70 signal, five-sector residual product, and preprocessing. We add an excluded-sector prediction test against smooth harmonic controls.
